rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will (tenancy at will termination notice)
rules.requirement: A landlord or tenant must give three months' written notice to end a tenancy at will (or the rent-payment interval or 30 days, whichever is longer, if rent is paid at intervals under three months). For nonpayment of rent, 14 days' written notice to quit is enough, but a tenant who has not had a similar notice in the prior 12 months can stop termination by paying all rent due within 10 days; the notice must include a statutory statement of that right.
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice (30 days min. if rent paid more often); 14 days' notice to quit for nonpayment, 10-day right to cure
rules.effective_date_note: Document gives no effective date for this long-standing section.
rules.penalty: If the notice omits the required cure-right notification, the tenant's time to pay or tender rent is extended to the day the answer is due in any possession action.

unverifiable_exemptions: applies only to tenancies at will, not fixed-term leases

parsed.doc_summary: Massachusetts G.L. c. 186, § 12 sets notice requirements to terminate tenancies at will: three months' notice (or 30 days/payment interval), and 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment with a 10-day cure right and required notice text.
